# Debian APT

<!-- Generated by tools/clientrecipes from src/debian.json; edit the source. -->

Read the [common setup and credential rules](README.md) first. [All recipes](index.md).

Client: **APT 3.3.3 (Ubuntu 26.10)**. Registered classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**.

Endpoint: `${AW_URL}/artifactory/${AW_REPO}`

## Before connecting

- A new Linux amd64 Ubuntu container; installation requires root inside that disposable container.
- Signed repository metadata and the corresponding trusted public key.
- AW_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY names the operator-verified ASCII-armored public key file; no private key belongs in the client container.

Authentication: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.

Fresh client state: Run in a newly created disposable pinned Ubuntu container and create AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d) inside it. Both the dpkg database and APT caches must be fresh; a fresh HOME alone is insufficient.

## Configure

Run this entire recipe inside a fresh disposable Ubuntu container. Verify the operator-provided public key before importing it. auth.conf is temporary and mode 0600. The public signing key and its parent directory are readable/traversable by the _apt sandbox; only the credential file stays private. Partial download directories belong to _apt.

```sh
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/lists/partial" "$AW_WORK/archives/partial"
cp "$AW_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY" "$AW_WORK/debian.asc"
printf 'deb [signed-by=%s/debian.asc] %s/artifactory/%s stable main\n' "$AW_WORK" "$AW_URL" "$AW_REPO" > "$AW_WORK/sources.list"
printf 'machine %s login %s password %s\n' "$AW_URL" "$AW_USER" "$AW_TOKEN" > "$AW_WORK/auth.conf"
chmod 0755 "$AW_WORK" "$AW_WORK/lists" "$AW_WORK/archives"
chmod 0644 "$AW_WORK/debian.asc" "$AW_WORK/sources.list"
chmod 0600 "$AW_WORK/auth.conf"
chown _apt:root "$AW_WORK/lists/partial" "$AW_WORK/archives/partial"
```

## Publish

Classes: **local, federated**. Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

The repository must have a signing key assigned. Matrix parameters select distribution, component and architecture.

```sh
curl --fail --silent --show-error --user "$AW_USER:$AW_TOKEN" --upload-file alpha_1.0_amd64.deb "$AW_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO/pool/main/a/alpha/alpha_1.0_amd64.deb;deb.distribution=stable;deb.component=main;deb.architecture=amd64"
```

## Install or resolve

Classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**. Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

APT still installs into the container system root: never run this install example on the host. The container must run as root.

```sh
aw_apt() { apt-get -o "Dir::Etc::sourcelist=$AW_WORK/sources.list" -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o "Dir::Etc::netrc=$AW_WORK/auth.conf" -o "Dir::State::lists=$AW_WORK/lists" -o "Dir::Cache::archives=$AW_WORK/archives" -o Acquire::Languages=none "$@"; }
aw_apt update
aw_apt install -y alpha
```

## Limits

Classes outside **local, remote, virtual, federated** are not registered for this format. Commands above apply only to each operation's listed classes. Federated evidence is for one node; it does not establish cross-vendor replication.

- The example is stable/main/amd64. Change distribution/component/architecture consistently.
- Fresh container state is required in addition to fresh lists and archive directories.
